statement: Failure of integer-degree harmonic dimension comparison. Disproves Yau's proposed Euclidean dimension bound for harmonic functions of integer growth on manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature. For every sufficiently large integer k, a complete smooth metric on ℝ3 has at least $`(k+2)^2`$ independent harmonic functions of growth at most k, exceeding the Euclidean count $`(k+1)^2`$. The metric may depend on k.
